text: Driver handover photos from the reefer van need the printed lot codes transcribed and sent back within a second or two while he's still standing at the door, but don't bump this ahead of other work, since the rush flag on the board is for the pharma van's job. Archiving the photos afterwards is allowed. Please run it on two mirrored nodes with failover and leave the hardware in eco mode.

hey can you run the north paddock drone footage and draw bounding boxes round every stray sheep? middle-of-the-road accuracy is plenty and there's no hurry on it, just let it grind through as a batch tonight, but put the compute in full-performance mode and keep a mirrored copy running in case a node falls over. oh and ignore the eco setting Dave used for his orchard flights last month, that's not for this one.

The Provider shall extract the printed characters from container manifest images captured at the inbound customs lane, and such jobs shall be placed ahead of routine work in the processing queue. Processing is not restricted to the checkpoint premises and may take place at an off-site data centre, and the Provider may retain the images and extracted results in storage. Each job shall execute on at least two mirrored instances with automatic failover and must finish within a fixed limit of 50 milliseconds per image. For clarity, the delete-on-completion rule that governs the outbound passenger lane does not apply to this Service.

Substation alert: thermal frames from the transformer yard need a bounding box drawn around every overheating bushing and clamp, using the most accurate model on offer. Frames must never leave the substation network; queue this as routine rather than escalated, run it on a paired failover instance, and return the boxes within about a second while the engineer watches the console. The escalation set by the protection team applies to their feeder job only.

Hey assistant, tally the yeast clumps in each sight-glass frame on fermenter three and just tell me the figure, as precisely as you possibly can. Don't keep the frames once they're counted, run it on two mirrored workers in full-power mode, and every frame has to be done inside a strict 20 millisecond cutoff. The brewer's request to archive footage was for the bottling line, not this tank.

Hi Marco,

For the orchard survey flights, could you set up a job that tallies the fallen fruit visible in each drone image and sends back only the total? Accuracy matters a lot here, so please use the most precise model we have. The images shouldn't be kept once they've been counted, and the job needs a failover twin running alongside it. It can run as an overnight batch; the per-frame deadline Lucy wanted is for her vineyard spraying project, not this one.

Thanks,
Jo

Charging hub bay feeds: box every car parked across two bays, sharpest detector we've got, and push it to the front of the queue. It doesn't have to run on the hub's own hardware, the cloud is fine, and keep the compute in power-saving mode. Attendants need results within a second or so on the tablet; the full-power profile the fleet depot asked for is their charger job.

quick one, can you pull the serial plate text off the fan motors in tunnel section 4 from the photos Sam took? bump it to the top of the pile, and keep it all on the tunnel control server, nothing goes offsite. fine to hang on to the pics afterwards, and one instance will do, we don't need the failover pair the signalling crew set up for their stuff.

The Operator requires that container ISO codes visible in spreader-mounted images be transcribed at the best achievable accuracy. Processing may be performed in the terminal's regional cloud tenancy rather than on the crane itself, and no image or derived output shall be kept beyond the moment the transcription is returned. The service shall run as two concurrently active replicas so that loss of one never interrupts operation, and results shall reach the crane driver's cab display within roughly one second of capture. The image archive held by the customs broker under its own agreement falls outside this clause and shall not be extended to this service.

Penguin enclosure feed: report just the head count of birds on the rocks for each frame, no boxes or labels needed. Frames can go up to the cloud for this one; the keep-it-onsite rule belongs to the veterinary clinic feed. Run in eco mode and meet a hard 100 ms per-frame deadline without exception.

Okay, read the tyre serial numbers off the photos from haul truck twelve, run-of-the-mill accuracy is fine, and make this a priority job. Keep everything on the mine's own servers, delete the photos as soon as they're read, and run it on two mirrored nodes. It doesn't have to come back live, a batch run later is okay; live results were what the dispatch team wanted for their own trucks.

Hi team,

We need bounding boxes drawn around every pedestrian and cyclist in the footage from the Main and 5th intersection, and please move this job ahead of everything else in the queue. Middling accuracy is acceptable, so there's no call for the premium model. Footage must be wiped once it's been processed, the job should run on a pair of mirrored instances, and the hardware should be pinned to its maximum-performance profile. The eco profile the parking enforcement group requested applies to their kerbside units only.

Regards,
Lena

Harvester head cam needs to transcribe the stamped numbers on each log end as it's cut, with top-tier accuracy because misreads scramble the log tracking. Keep processing on the machine's onboard unit, never over the satellite link, and run it power-saving. Each reading must land inside a hard 200 ms window; the relaxed overnight processing is the mill's scaling job, not this.

hey, need the number of vehicles in the tunnel bore from the portal feed, just a figure, and get it as precise as possible. it stays on the local control server, don't store the frames after, crank it to full power, and one instance is plenty. every frame has to finish under a strict 40 ms limit, and the mirrored setup the fire systems crew runs is theirs, not ours.

The Service shall report, for each X-ray scan of an inbound vehicle, solely the number of sealed packages present, with no positional or descriptive output. Baseline model accuracy is deemed sufficient, and computation may be carried out at the agency's remote data centre. One non-replicated instance operating in its power-conserving profile is acceptable, provided each result is returned within a hard deadline of 150 milliseconds. The dual-instance deployment specified for the passenger baggage line is not required under this clause.

Aisle 9 shelf scan ready: locate every misplaced product and outline it with a bounding box, using the top-accuracy model. Images must not leave the store's back-room server. Run in low-power mode on a primary plus hot standby, with each frame finished inside a strict 80 ms budget; the full-throttle profile belongs to the checkout lane's scanner, not this one.

Hey, find the parcels in the locker bay photos and draw a box around each one, regular accuracy is fine, and flag it as priority. It can go to the cloud, delete the photos once done, and keep the kiosk in battery-saver mode. One instance is enough, no failover, and it can run as a batch later; the live-response setting is for the courier app, not this.

Hello Farid,

Could you set the checkpoint scanner up to transcribe the machine-readable zone on each captured passport page? Please use the most accurate recognition model we licence, since a single wrong character causes a mismatch. There's no need for this to jump the queue, so the usual priority is fine; keep the unit in its eco profile, and a lone instance with no standby will do. The failover pair you configured for the cargo lane is a separate arrangement and shouldn't be copied over here.

Best,
Ana

AGV fleet: transcribe the rack location labels from yesterday's route photos, flagged top priority because the stocktake depends on it. Wipe each photo as soon as its label is read, and run the vehicles' compute at full power. Results can trickle through as a background batch, no live turnaround needed; the instant-response setting is for the picking robots' job.

can you tally the logs on the infeed deck from the inspection cam stills and just send back how many there are? no rush, it's a regular-queue thing, and it's ok to push it up to the cloud. bin the images once counted and run it on two mirrored nodes, the keep-everything archive is the grading team's thing, not ours.

The Contractor shall transcribe the fault codes and serial numbers shown in photographs of inverter display panels at the maximum attainable accuracy. All processing shall occur within the solar farm's own substation network, and no image or transcript may be kept once the corresponding output is delivered. One instance without standby, operating in its full-performance power profile, is sufficient, and results may be produced in scheduled batches rather than on demand. The dual-instance arrangement used for the grid-export metering service is excluded from this clause.

Pen 3 underwater feed: outline each fish showing lice lesions with a bounding box, best-accuracy model please, and jump this ahead of the queue. Cloud processing is fine here, frames get deleted right after analysis, and the node should run at full power. Don't apply the eco profile from the feed barge job, that setting was for their pumps.

Hey, mark every wilting seedling on the bench cameras with a box around it, using the sharpest model you've got. Run it flat out in performance mode on just one instance, no backup copy needed, and every frame has to finish inside a hard 30 millisecond limit. The mirrored pair is what the irrigation controller uses, not this job.

Hi Ravi,

We need the van's cargo camera to count the pallets loaded at each stop and send back just the figure. Please treat this as a priority job, since dispatch is waiting on the numbers. Images shouldn't be kept after counting, the job must have a live standby replica, and the unit should stay in its power-saving mode to protect the fridge battery. Drivers need the count on their handheld within a second or so, and the week-long image archive the returns team asked for is for their depot, not these vans.

Cheers,
Mel

Quay crane spreader cam: read the container numbers off the door-end images, with no compromise on accuracy. Offloading to the terminal cloud is fine, it doesn't have to be processed on the crane, and the compute should run at full throttle. The eco profile listed on the gantry's old work order was for last season's trial, not for this.

yo, can you read the ear-tag numbers off the giraffe yard shots, top accuracy please, and put it at the head of the queue? fine to send it to the cloud and keep the pics afterwards, one instance is enough without a backup. every frame needs to finish within a hard 50ms deadline, and ignore the delete-after rule from the reptile house job, that's theirs.

The Service shall return, for each deck image supplied by the bridge monitoring unit, only the number of heavy goods vehicles present on the span, without location data. Ordinary model accuracy is adequate, and processing may be performed at a remote facility away from the bridge. Requests shall be handled in the routine queue on one instance, with no standby instance required, and results shall be available to the monitoring engineer within approximately one second. The expedited handling granted to the maintenance contractor's crack survey is not extended to this Service.

Gantry 4B: place a bounding box around each vehicle's number plate region as cars pass under, flagged as priority. Captures must not be kept after processing, the job runs on an active pair with failover, and every frame must clear a hard 15 ms cutoff. The 30-day storage arrangement is for the enforcement unit's disputed-toll job, not this one.

Hey, count how many cereal boxes are left on the top shelf in aisle six and just give me the number. Don't hang on to the shelf photos afterwards, run it on two mirrored instances, and it's fine to do it in the overnight batch. Live counts are what the checkout team asked for, not this.

Hi Omar,

Please set up a job that marks every corrosion patch on the pipeline inspection images with a bounding box. It's a priority item, so it should go to the front of the queue. The images must not leave the plant's control network, though keeping them in storage afterwards is fine, and the unit should run at maximum performance. A single instance is sufficient here; the redundant pair belongs to the flare stack monitoring job.

Thanks,
Kai

Charging hub forecourt: box each abandoned trolley or cone blocking a bay in the overhead images. Regular queue is fine, it doesn't need priority, and processing can go to the cloud. Delete the images once the boxes are drawn; the 90-day keep rule is the security team's CCTV job, not this.

so can the harvester count the stems it fells from the boom cam and just report the number, as accurately as it can? keep it all on the machine's onboard computer, keeping the footage is fine, and it's not a rush job. run it full power on two mirrored units with a hard 100ms per-frame deadline, not the eco mode the forwarder crew uses.

The Service shall locate each skier's pass holder in the gate camera image and mark it with a bounding box, using the most accurate model available. Processing may be performed at the resort's remote data centre and shall be scheduled in the ordinary queue without preferential handling. One instance in power-saving mode is sufficient, provided every frame is completed within a hard 60 millisecond deadline. The priority scheduling applied to the ski patrol's avalanche beacon job shall not apply here.

Milking stall notice: outline each teat position with a bounding box in the robot arm's images so the cups line up. Everyday accuracy is fine, handle it in the regular queue, and nothing leaves the farm's own controller. Images are deleted once the cups are attached, and the job runs on a mirrored pair; the long-term footage store belongs to the herd health vet's job.

Hey, draw boxes around each meerkat in the burrow enclosure view. Keep the processing on the zoo's own server, not the cloud, run it in eco mode, and one instance is fine. The mirrored setup the aquarium team asked for is for their tank job, don't copy it.

Hi Sofia,

Can we get the greenhouse cameras boxing every tomato truss that shows blossom-end rot? It's a priority request, so please slot it ahead of the routine jobs. Cloud processing is fine, keeping the images on file is allowed, and the controller should run at full performance; its eco setting is only meant for the seedling house at night. Growers will be checking results on the tablet, so they need boxes back within a second or two.

Thanks,
Tom

Pipeline valve pit images: put bounding boxes on any visible leak stain, basic accuracy is fine, flagged priority. Storing the images is allowed, run it on a mirrored pair in power-saving mode, and each frame must finish inside a hard 100 ms deadline. Don't swap in the premium model the integrity engineers asked for, that one is for their weld audit.

need the crane cam to count the lashing bars on deck and just spit out the number, rough-and-ready accuracy's fine. priority job, keep it on the crane's own box, and bin the frames once counted. one instance, no failover needed, but each frame has to beat a hard 50ms deadline, and the other berth's cloud setup doesn't apply here.

The Provider shall transcribe the handwritten recipient names and unit numbers on parcels photographed at the locker kiosk, at the best accuracy the recognition model can achieve. Such jobs shall be queued ahead of routine work, and the Provider may keep the images and transcripts in storage. Processing on one instance is acceptable, and outputs may be delivered in periodic batches rather than on demand. The hot-standby configuration used for the payment terminal service shall not be applied to this Service.

Runway 16R sweep: box every piece of debris spotted on the pavement, adequate accuracy will do, routine priority. Frames can go to the cloud and be archived, run at full performance on one instance without a standby, and results need to reach the ops tablet within about a second. The rush flag belongs to the bird strike team's job.

Hey, how many people are queued at the north turnstiles right now? Just give me the number, counted as precisely as possible, and one instance is fine without any backup copy. I need the answer within a second or so; the mirrored setup is for the ticket scanners, not this.

Hi Grace,

Could you configure the kiosk so it counts the parcels sitting on the overflow shelf and reports only the total? This one can wait its turn in the ordinary queue, so there's no need to escalate it. Please run the kiosk hardware in performance mode, and each count must complete inside a hard 200 millisecond deadline. The power-saving schedule we set up last month was for the outdoor lockers, not this unit.

Thanks,
Ben

Toll gantry overhead images: box each truck's axle group for the class audit, priority job. Keeping the images is fine, run it on two mirrored instances in eco mode, and it doesn't need to be live, an overnight batch works; the per-vehicle live turnaround belongs to the enforcement lane.

can you read the gauge tag numbers in the flare deck photos, max accuracy, and put it top of the queue? keep it on the platform server, nothing goes ashore, delete the pics after reading, and run eco on one instance. each frame needs a hard 100ms deadline, and the mirrored pair is the drilling team's setup, not ours.

The Service shall transcribe the nameplate ratings from thermal and visible images of substation transformers at the best accuracy attainable. All processing shall remain within the substation's local network, and images shall not be kept once the transcription has been produced. The edge unit shall operate in its power-conserving profile. The full-performance profile specified for the protection relay analytics service does not apply to this clause.

Bus 212 door feed: draw a box around each child stepping off so the driver can confirm the kerb is clear, flagged as priority, and a mid-grade model is fine. Frames can be sent to the cloud, are deleted right after checking, and the job runs on two mirrored instances. Results must reach the driver's screen within about a second, not in the evening batch the route planning team uses.

Hey, read the meter numbers off today's pump station photos as accurately as you can. Keep it on the station's own server, it's fine to save the photos, and run the box at full performance. One instance is fine, it can run in the nightly batch, and don't use the failover pair, that's the SCADA team's setup.

Hi Jonas,

The AGVs need to read the printed text on each pallet label as they drive past, using our best recognition model. Please mark it as a priority job, since the dock is backed up. All processing stays inside the warehouse network with no cloud hop, although storing the label images afterwards is allowed. Every read must complete within a hard 25 millisecond deadline; the relaxed batch timing is only for the returns scanning job.

Best,
Priya

Fish pen sonar stills: box every net tear and loose float, best-accuracy model. Processing can go to the cloud, keeping the stills is fine, and one instance is enough, no failover. Run it as a background batch; the live response is for the feeding cam job only.

hey, can you box every e-scooter in yesterday's intersection clips, best accuracy you can get? run it flat out on max performance with a mirrored backup, and it can just go through as a batch overnight, no live results needed. the eco setting was for the bus lane job, not this.

The Service shall transcribe the digits shown on particle counter display panels photographed in each operating theatre. Baseline recognition accuracy is sufficient, and processing may take place at the hospital group's remote data centre. The edge device shall run in its maximum-performance mode on one instance, with no replica required, and each transcription shall be returned to the theatre nurse's terminal within roughly one second. The replicated deployment used for the anaesthesia monitoring service is outside the scope of this clause.

Fan room check: read the run-hour counter digits off each ventilation fan photo. Routine priority, not an escalation; images may be kept on file, and a single instance is enough. Results can come in the nightly batch, and the mirrored deployment listed on the jet-fan work order belongs to the fire damper job.

Hey, box every glove breach and gown gap you see on the cleanroom entry feed, so-so accuracy is fine, and make it a priority job. Keep it on the site server, nothing to the cloud, storing the clips is allowed, and run full performance. I need boxes back within a second while I'm at the airlock; the offsite processing the QA team uses is for their audit reports, not this.

Hi Lucas,

Please set up a job that draws bounding boxes around every patch of weeds in this week's drone survey of the canola fields. We want the most accurate model available, and the processing can happen in the cloud. The imagery may be kept for later comparison, and the drone's onboard compute should run at maximum performance. There's no need for live output, overnight batch processing is fine; the real-time feed is only for the spraying drone.

Thanks,
Hana

Northbound platform doors: box any bag or object left in the door gap from yesterday's recordings, regular priority, no need to escalate. Run it in full-performance mode and process as a background batch. The escalation flag on the board belongs to the southbound door fault job, not this.

can you read the tail numbers off aircraft taxiing past the runway cam, priority job please? cloud's fine for processing, delete the frames straight after, and one instance without a backup will do. each frame needs to finish inside a hard 80ms deadline, and the archive setting is for the noise team's job, not ours.

The Service shall mark each livestock animal visible in drone imagery of the grazing paddocks with a bounding box, and ordinary model accuracy shall be deemed adequate. Processing shall take place only on the farm's own base station and shall not be transferred to any off-farm facility. Jobs shall be placed in the routine queue and executed on two replicated instances in maximum-performance mode, and may be completed in scheduled batches. The expedited handling agreed for the neighbouring vineyard's frost-alert service does not form part of this clause.

Site gate scanner: report how many workers entered without a helmet, just the number, flagged as priority. Scans are deleted as soon as they're counted, the unit stays in battery-saver mode, and one instance is enough, no standby. The failover pair belongs to the crane zone scanner, not this gate.

Hey, count the round bales in the drone shots of the west field and just tell me the number, as accurately as you can. Keep it on the farm server, don't send it to the cloud, and keeping the photos is fine. No rush, regular queue, it can run in tonight's batch; the priority slot is the vet's herd scan, not this.

Hi Chris,

Could the watchtower camera put bounding boxes around any smoke plumes it picks up along the ridge line? Moderate accuracy is adequate, and this can go through the routine queue rather than being escalated. Processing can happen in the regional cloud, the footage should be erased once analysed, and the tower should stay in its solar-saving eco mode. Rangers want the boxes on their screen within a second or so; the all-footage archive is a separate request from the research station.

Regards,
Nina

Lane 2 X-ray: count the pallets in each truck scan and return the figure only. Scans can be kept on file, a single instance is fine with no failover, and each count must finish within a hard 120 ms deadline. The delete-after-scan rule is the passenger hall's policy, not this lane's.

can the arm's vision system box each bolt hole on the door panels, top accuracy please? don't keep the frames once processed, run it at full performance, and every frame has to finish inside a hard 10ms deadline. ignore the eco profile from the paint shop robots, that's their line.

The Service shall report only the number of fasteners present in each image of the assembly fixture, without positional output, and baseline model accuracy is acceptable. Processing shall remain on the plant's own line controller, and images may be retained. Jobs shall receive priority over routine work and run on one instance in maximum-performance mode, with results displayed to the line operator within approximately one second. The standby replica specified for the welding cell service is not required here.

Feed barge panel: read the hopper weight digits shown in each photo, workable accuracy is fine, routine priority. Processing stays on the barge computer, never sent ashore, and the unit runs at full performance. Readings should reach the farmhand's phone within a second; the power-saving profile is for the solar buoy sensors, not this.

Hey, read the worker ID stickers off the helmets in today's gate photos, priority job. Keep it on the site office server, not the cloud, run it full power on a mirrored pair, and a batch run later is fine. Live results were for the scaffold crew's scanner, not this one.

Hi Dev,

The pole-mounted cameras need to transcribe the registration plates of vehicles parked in the loading zones overnight. Adequate accuracy is sufficient, and please flag it as a priority job for the enforcement team. Everything must be processed on the pole's own edge node, the images deleted once read, and the job run on a mirrored pair. Results can come through in the morning batch rather than live; the live stream was the traffic signal team's request.

Cheers,
Maya

Bus fleet cabin cams: count the passengers seated on each bus and send back the number only, the default model is fine. Cloud processing is allowed, run at full performance on one instance without a standby, and each count has to land inside a hard 200 ms deadline. The eco profile noted on last term's setup doesn't apply to this.

can you box every carton that's tipped over in the reefer's cargo cam shots? keep it on the van's onboard unit, not the cloud, and saving the shots is fine. no rush, regular queue, one instance, and it can run as a batch after the route; the live feed is the depot's thing.

The Service shall report only the number of students boarding at each stop, derived from the bus door camera footage. Processing may occur at the operator's remote cloud platform, and footage shall not be kept after each count is produced. The Service shall run in the vehicle unit's power-saving mode on two mirrored instances with automatic failover, and each count shall be completed within a hard deadline of 250 milliseconds. The footage archive maintained by the transport safety auditor is governed by a separate agreement and is excluded.

Switchyard feed: box every bird nest on the gantry structures, top-accuracy model please, routine priority with no escalation. Frames may be sent to the cloud and kept on file, and the job runs on a mirrored pair. Engineers need boxes back within a second or two; the priority flag in the queue belongs to the breaker fault job.
Hey, how many bags are sitting in the compactor bin right now? Just the number, no hurry, and keep the unit in eco mode rather than the full-power setting the depot uses on its trucks.

Hi Ellie,

Could the harvester's cab system count the logs stacked on each forwarder load and show just the total? Modest accuracy is fine, and everything should stay on the machine's own computer. Keeping the images afterwards is allowed, the unit should run in its fuel-saving eco mode, and one instance is sufficient without any backup. The operator needs the count within a second or so; the mirrored setup you mentioned is for the mill's scaling station.

Thanks,
Rob

Reefer van door labels: transcribe the batch and expiry codes from each loading photo, best accuracy available. Process only on the van's onboard unit, no uploads, and the photos may be kept. Run it in eco mode on a mirrored pair; the delete-after-read setting was for the grocery vans last month, not this route.

can you read the boarding pass numbers off the gangway scanner images, top accuracy, and put it at the front of the queue? saving the images is fine, run the box flat out on max performance, and each frame needs to finish under a hard 50ms deadline. don't use the eco mode the car deck team set, that's for their scanners.

The Service shall report only the number of passengers waiting at each platform screen door, at the best accuracy available. Processing shall occur solely on the station's local server, and footage may be retained. Jobs shall be given priority in the queue and the edge unit shall operate in power-saving mode, with results delivered in periodic batches rather than per frame. The strict per-frame deadline specified for the door obstruction service does not apply here.

Inverter bank 5: read the fault code off each display photo, a basic model is fine, routine queue. Keep processing inside the farm network with nothing sent offsite, run at full performance, and each read must meet a hard 100 ms deadline. The eco profile on the tracker motors is a separate job.

Hey, count the knots on each board in the latest inspection shots and just give me the number, rough accuracy is fine. It can go to the cloud, no rush, keep the images, and run it at full performance. The eco setting was for the kiln sensors, not this.

Hi Tariq,

Please configure the robotic arm's camera to read the VIN stamped on each chassis rail as it passes the station. We need the most accurate recognition model available. The vision unit should run in its eco profile, and the job must not run as a lone instance, so keep a mirrored copy ready to take over on failure. Each read has to complete within a hard 20 millisecond deadline; the full-power profile is for the welding cell, not this station.

Best,
Lin

Blade inspection drone: box each leading-edge erosion spot on the blade images, best-accuracy model. Cloud processing allowed, images can be kept, run eco on one instance with no failover, and each frame must meet a hard 150 ms deadline. The full-power profile is the tower climb team's setting, not this flight.

can you count the kegs on the cold room racks from the camera stills and just send me the number? priority job, keep it all on the brewery server, nothing to the cloud, and saving the stills is fine. run it on a mirrored pair, the single-box setup is for the taproom stuff, not this.

The Service shall transcribe gauge readings and equipment tags from engine room inspection images at the best accuracy attainable. All processing shall take place on the vessel's onboard server and shall not be transmitted ashore, and images shall be deleted once transcribed. The Service shall run on two replicated instances with failover and may deliver results in scheduled batches. The strict per-frame deadline specified for the propulsion alarm service does not apply to this clause.

Tower 9 feed: read the registration on any vehicle stopped near the fire trail gate, a basic model will do, routine priority. Frames aren't kept once read, the unit runs at full performance, and results must reach the ranger's tablet within a second. The eco schedule belongs to the radio repeater, not this.

Hey, read the lot numbers off the vial trays in the filling room photos, as accurately as you can. Keep the unit in eco mode, one instance without a backup is fine, and it can run as an overnight batch. The live readout is what the sterility team wanted, not this.

Hi Anika,

Could you set up the substation camera to draw bounding boxes around any hotspots on the busbar joints? Please use the most precise model we have, and queue it as routine work since it isn't an escalation. The unit should run at maximum performance with a mirrored instance for failover, and boxes need to reach the control room display within a second or so. The eco profile belongs to the pole-top cameras on the feeder lines, not this one.

Kind regards,
Joel

Spray drone: read the chemical batch labels on the tank photos, entry-level accuracy, flagged priority. Keep processing on the farm base station, no cloud, and the photos may be stored. Results back to the pilot's controller within a second; the premium model is for the agronomist's yield job.

can the truck's cab unit read the load docket numbers off the dash photos? decent accuracy's fine, no rush, keep it on the mine's own network, and run it at full power. each read needs a hard 100ms deadline, and ignore the priority flag, that's the blasting crew's job.

The Service shall mark each concealed compartment identified in vehicle X-ray images with a bounding box, and baseline model accuracy is sufficient. Jobs shall be handled in the routine queue, and images shall not be kept after analysis. The Service shall run on two replicated instances with failover, returning results to the inspecting officer within approximately one second. The evidentiary image archive maintained for the seizure unit is outside the scope of this clause.

Particle counter log: read the printed readings off each photographed printout, entry-level accuracy, flagged priority. Keep the unit in eco mode, and results can arrive in the next batch rather than live. The top-accuracy model is reserved for the QA release team's review.

Hey, how many floating debris clumps are on the inlet screen right now? Just the number, ordinary accuracy is fine, and no rush. Keep it on the station server, not the cloud, run eco on a mirrored pair, and get it back within a second; the full-power setting is the blower room's.

Hi Paolo,

We need the intersection cameras to count the vehicles turning right on red and report just the totals. Reasonable accuracy is fine, and please mark it as priority since council wants the figures this week. Keep all processing on the roadside cabinet, not the cloud, delete the footage once counted, and run the cabinet at maximum performance. A batch run is fine; the live counts are the transit signal team's request.

Thanks,
Ines

Ward 4 bedside cams: box any patient sitting up at the bed edge as a fall risk, best accuracy model, priority. Processing can go to the hospital's remote data centre, clips may be stored, and run eco. Each frame needs a hard 100 ms deadline, not the batch timing the audit team uses.

can you count the birds on the runway in each frame and just give me the number, as accurate as possible? cloud processing is fine, don't keep the frames after, and each frame needs a hard 60ms deadline. the keep-everything archive is the wildlife team's, not ours.

The Service shall mark each rail crack and missing clip in track inspection images with a bounding box.
